The temperature sensor accepts readings from minus 20 to 60 degrees Celsius. Values outside this range are rejected.

The sensor reports temperature every 30 seconds while connected to external power.

On battery power the sensor reports once every five minutes.

The sensor stores up to 500 readings while offline. The oldest reading is replaced when storage is full.

An amber indicator means the battery is below 15 percent.

A red indicator means the temperature probe is disconnected.

The sensor uses two AA batteries. Rechargeable AA batteries are supported.

Factory reset removes stored readings and Wi-Fi credentials.

Hold the reset button for ten seconds to start a factory reset.

The calibration offset can be set between minus 3 and plus 3 degrees Celsius.

The enclosure is rated for indoor use. It must not be exposed to rain.

Each exported reading includes a UTC timestamp and a temperature in degrees Celsius.

Ordinary support messages are deleted after 30 days. This rule has an exception
described on the following page; consult that exception before answering questions
about legal holds.

Exception to the ordinary support-message retention rule: messages under an
active legal hold are kept until the hold is released, even after 30 days.

Financial invoices are retained for seven years from their issue date.

An export request includes active records and archived records, but excludes
records already deleted.

Only compliance administrators can apply a legal hold.

Releasing a legal hold requires two different compliance administrators to approve
the release.

Deleting an account disables sign-in immediately. Record retention continues under
the applicable retention rules.

An audit event records the actor, UTC time, and record identifier for every deletion.

Attachments follow the retention period of the message to which they belong.

A retention preview lists records scheduled for deletion during the next 24 hours.

Changing a retention policy affects future deletion decisions and does not restore
records already deleted.

The retention service pauses deletion when its policy database is unavailable.

The green status light means the printer is ready.

The blue status light means the printer is receiving a job.

The orange status light means the paper tray is empty.

Use A4 or Letter plain paper in the main tray.

The main tray holds at most 150 sheets.

Envelopes must be fed one at a time through the rear slot.

To cancel the active print job, hold Cancel for two seconds.

Cleaning the rollers requires disconnecting the power cable first.

The printer enters sleep mode after ten minutes without a job.

Press any control-panel button to wake the printer from sleep.

The printer rejects jobs protected by an unsupported encryption format.

A client sends a monotonically increasing sequence number with every update. A lower sequence number is rejected.

When the same sequence number and payload are received twice, the server returns the original acknowledgement without applying the update again.

The maximum update payload is 64 KiB.

A payload larger than 64 KiB receives status 413.

The server responds with status 409 when the same sequence number is reused with different content.

An acknowledgement contains the committed sequence number.

Clients retry transient failures with exponential backoff, starting at one second and capped at one minute.

Authentication failures are not retried automatically.

The sync cursor expires after seven days without use.

An expired cursor requires a full snapshot before incremental updates resume.

Each response includes a request identifier for diagnostic correlation.

An update is considered durable only after the acknowledgement has been received.

controls.reference: Clients use exponential backoff starting at one second and capped at one minute.

controls.response: Retry exponentially, starting at 1 second and never exceeding 60 seconds.

Items marked fragile must be packed with foam inserts.

A parcel may weigh at most 20 kilograms for the standard courier service.

Parcels over 20 kilograms must use the freight service.

Orders received before 14:00 on a working day are dispatched that day.

Orders received at or after 14:00 are dispatched on the next working day.

A missing item blocks dispatch of the entire order until the discrepancy is resolved.

A supervisor must approve replacing an ordered item with an alternative.

Returned electronic items go to inspection before they can be restocked.

The packing slip contains item names and quantities but excludes payment-card details.

Damaged stock is placed in the quarantine area and cannot be allocated to orders.

The dispatch scan records the parcel identifier and courier tracking number.

A cancelled order must not be dispatched even if a shipping label has already been printed.

Rollback restores the previously deployed application version.

Rollback does not reverse database migrations.

A database backup is required before a deployment that includes a migration.

Deployment logs are retained for 14 days.

A maintenance window prevents automatic deployments from starting.

A deployment already in progress continues when a maintenance window begins.

controls.source:
The application follows a consistent interaction model across its settings, editor, and review screens. Keyboard focus remains visible so a user can tell which control receives input. Pressing Tab moves focus to the next enabled control. Disabled controls are skipped in this navigation sequence.

Within a group of radio buttons, arrow keys change the selected option. Tab moves out of the radio group to the next control. This behavior avoids requiring a separate Tab stop for every option and preserves predictable navigation.

A modal dialog keeps keyboard focus inside the dialog until it closes. Closing the dialog returns focus to the control that opened it. A dialog that cannot identify its opener returns focus to the first enabled control in the main window.

Every icon-only action exposes an accessible name describing the action. Decorative icons do not expose separate accessible elements. An icon that conveys status must have an accessible text description of that status.

Error messages identify the affected field and explain how to correct the problem. The application announces a newly displayed error to assistive technology. It does not clear the current field value when reporting an error.

Long-running actions expose a textual progress description. When the total amount of work is unknown, the description reports that processing is active without inventing a completion percentage.

Cancelling a long-running import keeps previously saved work. Partial unsaved import content is discarded. The application announces that cancellation has completed after the import task has actually stopped.

Text enlargement increases interface text size without hiding essential actions. When content no longer fits vertically, the panel scrolls. The primary action remains reachable through keyboard navigation.

Color is never the only way to communicate validation status. A failed field includes a textual explanation in addition to its color treatment. A successful field may include an icon with an accessible description.

The reduced-motion setting replaces animated panel transitions with immediate state changes. This setting does not disable progress announcements or hide the result of an action.

Screen-reader reading order follows the visual order of labels, controls, and help text. Related help text is associated with its control. A field label is announced before its current value.

A destructive confirmation identifies the item to be deleted. The default keyboard action is Cancel. Pressing Return without changing focus therefore cancels the confirmation.

Workspace exports are available to owners. Members can view reports but cannot export a workspace.

Guests may read published reports. Guests cannot edit report drafts.

An invitation link expires 48 hours after it is created.

A workspace may contain at most 25 active members.

Only an owner can delete a workspace. Deletion requires entering the workspace name.

Archived workspaces are read-only. Restoring a workspace makes it editable again.

Owners can rotate an API key. Rotating a key immediately revokes the previous key.

A failed sign-in is recorded in the audit log. Audit records are retained for 90 days.

Removing a member ends their workspace access immediately. Their existing reports remain in the workspace.

A workspace name must contain between 3 and 60 characters.

Changing the workspace time zone affects future scheduled reports, not reports already generated.

A transfer of ownership must be accepted by the new owner before the old owner loses that role.

The temperature sensor accepts readings from minus 20 to 60 degrees Celsius. Values outside this range are rejected.

The sensor reports temperature every 30 seconds while connected to external power.

On battery power the sensor reports once every five minutes.

The sensor stores up to 500 readings while offline. The oldest reading is replaced when storage is full.

An amber indicator means the battery is below 15 percent.

A red indicator means the temperature probe is disconnected.

The sensor uses two AA batteries. Rechargeable AA batteries are supported.

Factory reset removes stored readings and Wi-Fi credentials.

Hold the reset button for ten seconds to start a factory reset.

The calibration offset can be set between minus 3 and plus 3 degrees Celsius.

The enclosure is rated for indoor use. It must not be exposed to rain.

Each exported reading includes a UTC timestamp and a temperature in degrees Celsius.

A room booking may last at most four hours.

Bookings can be made up to 30 days in advance.

A booking can be cancelled without a charge until two hours before its start.

Cancelling less than two hours before the start incurs a ten-credit charge.

Check in within 15 minutes of the start time. Otherwise the room is released.

Guests need a host present throughout the booking.

Food is permitted in rooms A and B. Food is prohibited in room C.

The projector must be requested when the booking is created.

A recurring booking can include up to eight weekly occurrences.

Changing a recurring booking affects only the selected occurrence unless all future
occurrences are selected.

Room B accommodates six people. The occupancy limit must not be exceeded.

The booking receipt is sent to the organizer, not to every attendee.

Ordinary support messages are deleted after 30 days. This rule has an exception
described on the following page; consult that exception before answering questions
about legal holds.

Exception to the ordinary support-message retention rule: messages under an
active legal hold are kept until the hold is released, even after 30 days.

Financial invoices are retained for seven years from their issue date.

An export request includes active records and archived records, but excludes
records already deleted.

Only compliance administrators can apply a legal hold.

Releasing a legal hold requires two different compliance administrators to approve
the release.

Deleting an account disables sign-in immediately. Record retention continues under
the applicable retention rules.

An audit event records the actor, UTC time, and record identifier for every deletion.

Attachments follow the retention period of the message to which they belong.

A retention preview lists records scheduled for deletion during the next 24 hours.

Changing a retention policy affects future deletion decisions and does not restore
records already deleted.

The retention service pauses deletion when its policy database is unavailable.

Control-S saves the active document without changing its file name.

Control-Shift-S opens Save As for the active document.

Control-Z undoes the most recent edit.

Control-Y redoes an edit that was undone.

The editor autosaves every 60 seconds while the document has unsaved changes.

Autosave does not run for documents opened in read-only mode.

The recovery panel offers the most recent autosaved version after an unexpected exit.

Closing a document with unsaved changes prompts the user to save, discard, or cancel closing.

Find searches only the active document. Find in Folder searches all supported files in the chosen folder.

The line-number display can be toggled from the View menu.

The editor preserves UTF-8 encoding when saving a UTF-8 text file.

Tabs are displayed as four spaces by default; this setting changes display width without rewriting the file.

controls.source:
The draft release note says uploads are limited to 8 MB. A second equally authoritative draft says uploads are limited to 12 MB. No approved limit is supplied.

Release 4.2 adds a progress indicator to uploads.

Release 4.2 fixes a crash when cancelling an upload.

Uploads paused by the user do not resume automatically after relaunch.

The retry button restarts the failed upload from the beginning.

Upload filenames are preserved in the destination folder.

The destination folder must be writable before an upload can begin.

An interrupted network connection leaves the upload in the Failed state.

A completed upload shows the destination path in its details.

The upload history retains the latest 100 jobs.

Removing a job from history does not delete its uploaded file.

The upload queue runs two jobs concurrently.
